newsitem.title: USA: US Midwest direct hog prices seen mixed - dealers.
newsitem.headline: US Midwest direct hog prices seen mixed - dealers.

text.p: U.S. Midwest direct cash hog prices Wednesday were seen mixed, depending on hog availability, livestock dealers said.
Prices were seen steady to $1.00 per cwt higher in the eastern Corn Belt as hog supplies start tightening, and $0.50 to $1.00 lower in the west on continued adequate receipts, they said.

Top prices for interior Iowa and southern Minnesota hogs delivered to the plant could range $50.00 to $50.50. Illinois top hog prices at the plant could range $50.00 to $50.50. Indiana/Ohio top hog prices could range $51.00 to $52.00.
Packer demand remained light on Tuesday as pork prices continued to sag, dealers said.

Fresh loin prices at midday were quoted down $2.00 per cwt, hams were $2.00 to $5.00 lower and bellies were $1.00 to $4.00 lower, USDA said. There were 45 pork loads and 27.5 loads of trimmed pork sold, USDA said.
However, light slaughter this week due to Presidents' Day holiday on Monday could underpin cash pork, sources said.
Slaughter Tuesday was estimated at 342,000 head, which brought the week-to-date figure to 623,000, compared with 650,000 a week ago and 660,000 a year ago.
